findings.description: Row cardinality/order: SHEET-TAB-005 says only 'populate ... per (Jurisdiction, Tax Year) from tax::annual_report's figures' — silent on ordering or on how rows relate to the input structure. The real code's render_tax(accruals: &[Accrual], annual_rows: &[AnnualRow]) -> TaxView builds reserve_rows by a single 'for r in annual_rows' loop with NO sort, NO group-by-key, NO dedup — one row per slice element, in the caller's exact order (test reserve_summary_carries_all_five_kernel_exact_columns even zips tax.reserve_summary.rows.iter().zip(annual.iter()) positionally, and asserts rows.len() == annual.len()). All three B outputs pin this identically (B1 #1; B2 'Provenance'; B3 #2). Notably, all three A-side sketches — working from the EARS text alone — unanimously invented a defensive sort_by(jurisdiction.then(tax_year)) pass 'for deterministic sheet output,' which the real code does not do. That invented sort has no basis in the spec text (EARS never mentions ordering), so per the classification rule it is an assumption artifact, not an A-finding — but it is the concrete place a from-spec-alone implementer would diverge from the pinned behavior.

Cents string-formatting contract: the EARS says the five figures are 'consumed as pure values' (an accounting-semantics statement — no recomputation), but says nothing about how a Cents value renders as text. The real fmt_cents helper fixes an exact algorithm — sign only if negative, whole = abs/100, frac = abs%100 zero-padded to 2 digits, e.g. Cents(15000) -> "150.00" — and the test literally re-implements the same closure to assert equality cell-by-cell. All 3 B outputs converge on the identical formula (B1 #4, B2 'Formatting/normalization', B3 #4).

Engine-value-only / never-formula guarantee: the EARS's 'consumed as pure values, holding no tax math' is about accounting math, not about the sheet's engine-value-vs-formula cell typing. The code enforces a separate, additional structural rule — every cell in reserve_summary (and accruals) is Cell::Value, never Cell::Formula — tested explicitly by tax_tab_is_kernel_exact_not_live_formula ('Tax tab must be kernel-exact values, found a formula'). All 3 B outputs pin this (B1 #3, B2 'Value typing', B3 #6), each explicitly contrasting it with the Positions tab's GOOGLEFINANCE-formula columns — a contrast the EARS text never draws.

Jurisdiction/Tax Year label rendering: the EARS never specifies how the key columns render as text. Code fixes jurisdiction_label (Jurisdiction::Federal -> "Federal", Jurisdiction::State(code) -> "State({code})") and renders Tax Year as the bare decimal integer. All 3 B outputs pin this identically (B1 #5/#6, B2, B3 #7/#8), and it is directly exercised by the test's "Federal"/"2022" string assertions.

Header/tab structural contract: the EARS names the five figures plus the (Jurisdiction, Tax Year) key conceptually, but never states literal header text, column order, or tab naming. Code fixes TAX_RESERVE_HEADER = ["Jurisdiction","Tax Year","Accrued","Moved","Paid","Outstanding","Shortfall"] and TAX_RESERVE_TAB = "Tax · Reserve Summary", and keeps the band structurally distinct (own ViewTab) from the accrual band (TAX_HEADER/TAX_TAB) so neither carries embedded/blank summary rows. All 3 B outputs pin the exact header list/order and the band-separation rule (B1 #8, B2 'Header/columns', B3 #9/#10).

Completeness/no-blank-cell rule: the EARS doesn't address what happens for a true zero balance. The code+test explicitly guarantee none of the five figure cells is ever an empty string — a zero renders "0.00", never blank — per the test's own comment 'the gap the review flagged.' All 3 B outputs pin this as an explicit unwanted-behavior requirement (B1 #7, B2 'Completeness', B3 #5).

Minor, single-run finding: render_tax returns TaxView directly (no Result/ViewError), unlike render_positions's Result<ViewTab, ViewError> with its DuplicateSymbolRow guard — there is no analogous duplicate-(Jurisdiction,TaxYear) guard on the reserve-summary path. This is true of the real signature but was surfaced by only B2 ('No failure path'), not B1 or B3, so it's flagged with lower confidence than the items above.

notes: Direction A (A1/A2/A3), reconstructing from the EARS text alone, converges tightly on the substance the spec actually states — a pure pass-through of five Cents figures keyed by (Jurisdiction, Tax Year), no computation, no validation of malformed upstream data — and this matches the real code faithfully. Where the three A outputs diverge is purely in how they modeled the unstated tax::annual_report input shape (A1: &[AnnualReportLine]; A2: &BTreeMap<(Jurisdiction,TaxYear), AnnualReportFigures>; A3: &AnnualReport with .entries()) — none matches the real &[AnnualRow] slice parameter to render_tax, but none of the three explicitly claims a specific API shape as spec-mandated (each flags it as an invented assumption), so this isn't scored as an A-finding. The one substantive unanimous A invention — sorting rows by (Jurisdiction, Tax Year) for 'deterministic output' — actively contradicts the real code's caller-order-preserving behavior, but has zero textual basis in the EARS, so per the classification rules it's an assumption artifact rather than a scored A-side finding; it is, however, a nice illustration of exactly the row-order axis that Direction B independently flags as code-side surplus. No direction-A finding traces to explicit spec text and is missing from the real code, so the audit nets out to B-only: the code and tests pin a long list of concrete rendering/typing/structural rules (cents formatting, jurisdiction label, header text, no-formula/value-only typing, no-blank-cell completeness, row-order/cardinality-preservation, and — per one B run only — the lack of a Result/duplicate-key guard) that SHEET-TAB-005's spare EARS text never states.
